definition: The system of moving people or goods from one place to another.
example: Buses and trains are the main forms of public transport.
note: All three original translations were the thing itself and had been changed into the action. In British English the first meaning of 'transport' is the system, as in 'public transport'. Restored.

definition: A railway that runs in tunnels below a city.
example: We took the underground to the city centre.
note: The definition described the city railway, but Spanish and French gave words meaning 'below the ground', which is a different idea. Both changed to the word for the railway so all four match.

definition: The system of linked pages on the internet.
example: You can find the answer on the web.
note: Had been changed to mean a spider's web, with the awkward example 'A big web is on the tree'. Three of the four original translations were the internet, which is what 'web' means to anyone today. Restored.

definition: Doing a job or making an effort.
example: I am working now.
note: The four languages were in four different shapes. They now all use the same '-ing' form.

definition: To feel anxious about something.
example: I worry about my exams tomorrow.
note: German was missing the reflexive part that the other three all have.

definition: Belonging to you.
example: This book is yours.
note: French gave the polite plural form while the other three gave the friendly singular. Changed to 'le tien' so they match.

definition: Very old.
example: The aged man walked slowly with a stick.
note: Had been narrowed to the special meaning used for cheese and wine. All three original translations simply meant 'old', which is the first meaning of 'aged'. Restored.

definition: To help someone.
example: Could you assist me with these heavy bags, please?
note: Spanish 'asistir' and Italian 'assistere' are false friends: they mean 'to attend' or 'to be present at', not 'to help'. Both corrected.

definition: To cook food such as bread or cakes in an oven.
example: She will bake a delicious cake for the party.
note: French 'cuire' on its own just means 'to cook'. Adding 'au four' makes it baking, matching the Italian.

definition: The air you take into and let out of your lungs.
example: Take a deep breath and relax your body.
note: The example was broken ('relax your body will relax'). Cleaned up.

definition: A person or team that wins a competition.
example: She is the world champion in swimming.
note: Had been changed to mean someone who supports a cause, and all four translations were also switched to women-only forms. Every original translation was 'the winner', which is the first meaning of 'champion'. Fully restored.

definition: A separate part of a contract or legal document.
example: The contract has a clause about late payment.
note: All four translations mean a part of a contract, but the definition described a grammar term and the example did not even contain the word 'clause'. Definition and example now match the translations.

definition: Having a colour, or more than one colour.
example: She drew the picture with bright coloured pencils.
note: The headword is a describing word but the entry taught it as the action 'to colour something in'. Everything now describes objects that have colour.

definition: Happy and satisfied with what you have.
example: She felt content with her warm tea and a good book.
note: French and Italian were in the women-only form. Changed to the standard form, matching Spanish and German.

definition: A clear difference between two things.
example: There is a big contrast between the two paintings.
note: All three original translations were the thing itself and had been changed into the action. 'A contrast' is the first meaning. Restored.

definition: Having something placed over the top.
example: The baby was covered with a warm blanket.
note: Spanish gave the plain action word while the other three gave the describing form that matches the headword. Spanish corrected and the example changed so it describes rather than acts.

definition: An agreement, especially in business.
example: The two companies made a deal to work together.
note: Had been narrowed to handing out playing cards. The first meaning of 'deal' is an agreement, which is what the original French showed. Rebuilt around that.

definition: Going straight from one place to another without stopping.
example: We took a direct flight to Rome with no stops.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: Twice as much or twice as many.
example: He ordered a double portion of ice cream.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: To let something fall by accident.
example: Please be careful, do not drop the plate.
note: The example was broken ('do not drop the plate. I gave you.'). Cleaned up and matched to the other 'drop' entry.

definition: A person who checks and corrects writing before it is published.
example: The editor corrected mistakes in the newspaper article.
note: Italian 'editore' means the publisher, the company that sells the book. The person who checks the writing is a 'redattore'.

definition: Having agreed to marry someone.
example: They got engaged and will marry next year.
note: Had been changed to the vaguer meaning 'busy doing something'. The first meaning of 'engaged' is about to be married, which is what the original Spanish and French showed. Restored.

definition: Relating to the natural world around us.
example: We need to protect the environmental health of our planet.
note: German 'ökologisch' means ecological, which is narrower. The direct match is 'Umwelt-'.
